methods.openingPopulationDefinition: IPEDS 2021–22 published nonresident degree totals aligned with, but not linked to, FY2022 SEVIS starts.
methods.compensationRule: A matched record would continue when its FY2022 benchmark total compensation is at least as large as the reader-selected fee.
methods.occupationInference: The genuine first post-completion job title is matched through audited title × CIP and global overrides, exact O*NET titles, and safe deterministic normalization constrained by the official CIP–SOC crosswalk. When six-digit matching remains unresolved, a separate broad-family benchmark is used only when an interpretable title phrase and the crosswalk agree on one SOC major group. The provisional fuzzy method failed its fixed precision thresholds and is not used in candidate outcomes. Records without usable titles and unresolved generic titles remain unknown; later jobs are never substituted.
methods.programOutcome: Expected program end from 2021-07-01 through 2022-06-30; first post-completion OPT start linked to the same STUDENT_KEY and occurring within 60 days; minimum 50 expected-completion records.

compensationCoverage.matchMethod: exact unique O*NET title; no FY2022 OEWS benchmark

sources.dataset: U.S. Weighs $100,000 Fee for Foreign Students Wanting to Work After Graduation
sources.local_input: Policy assumption documented in analysis code and narratives
sources.transformation: Model one $100,000 charge when a graduate seeks access to post-completion OPT; do not model a second STEM-extension charge; treat student-paid and employer-paid designs as alternative payer scenarios
sources.limitations: News report describes an administration proposal under consideration; no public proposed rule specifies the fee, payer, timing, exemptions, refundability, or implementation details

sources.dataset: Policy Manual Volume 2 Part F Chapter 5 — Practical Training
sources.local_input: Official guidance cited in the story orientation
sources.transformation: Use to define degree-related practical training, up to 12 months of post-completion OPT, and the possible 24-month STEM OPT extension
sources.use: Explain how OPT connects an F-1 student's degree to temporary U.S. work
sources.limitations: Eligibility and authorization are individualized; the story models initial post-completion OPT entry and does not model a second fee for the STEM extension

sources.dataset: Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS)
sources.transformation: Data requested by the Institute for Progress under FOIA; use corrected filename as fiscal year; parse authorization dates; select each person's first post-completion start within that file; deduplicate within file only
sources.limitations: Event log; identifiers cannot link across annual files; extensive missingness; file inclusion rule is not documented by ICE

sources.local_input: Documentation and public distribution of ICE FOIA release #43657
sources.transformation: Credit Violet Buxton-Walsh and Jeremy Neufeld; retain ICE as the underlying data producer and the Institute for Progress as the FOIA requester
sources.limitations: The Observatory documents and distributes administrative records; it is not the original data producer

sources.dataset: The Impact of Immigration on the Labor Market Outcomes of Native Workers
sources.transformation: Describe the paper's reported small negative effects on native earnings and employment; identify the study as immigration-wide rather than OPT-specific
sources.limitations: Working paper studies immigration broadly and does not identify OPT participants

sources.dataset: Creation or Destruction? STEM OPT Extension and Employment of Information Technology Professionals
sources.transformation: Describe the reported increase in domestic STEM employment following the STEM OPT extension, with stronger effects in IT
sources.limitations: Study estimates aggregate occupation effects and cannot determine the outcome of every individual hiring decision

sources.dataset: OPT Reforms and the Relative Supply of STEM Skills
sources.transformation: Describe the reported increase in domestic STEM degree completions after OPT expansions as suggestive of crowd-in
sources.limitations: Paper studies degree completion rather than employment and describes the result as suggestive

sources.dataset: SEVIS Form I-20 financial information guide
sources.transformation: Sum positive reported personal, school, other, and on-campus funding fields; preserve missingness when every component is missing
sources.use: Interpret reported tuition and annual educational funding
sources.limitations: Administrative Form I-20 amounts are neither audited wealth nor liquid funds

sources.transformation: Select reported graduate nonresident tuition and required fees; compare to SEVIS median by school/campus
sources.limitations: Institution-level sticker price can differ from program price and the SEVIS record's reporting period

sources.transformation: Use the published nonresident bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral totals for the opening population; retain program completions only as an external methods comparison
sources.use: Opening population and external denominator check
sources.limitations: IPEDS awards and FY2022 SEVIS authorization starts are aligned annual flows rather than linked people; IPEDS is not the headline school-program denominator

sources.transformation: Apply audited title × CIP and global overrides; exact O*NET matching; terminal-level/status and abbreviation normalization; then provisional fuzzy matching only at WRatio >=96, ordinary ratio >=90, and a >=7-point distinct-SOC margin
sources.use: Map SEVIS job titles to occupations
sources.limitations: Sparse and nonstandard SEVIS titles; generic titles remain unresolved; all provisional fuzzy matches were demoted after the fixed validation sample missed the required precision

sources.transformation: Collapse O*NET decimal suffix to six-digit SOC for OEWS joins
sources.limitations: O*NET and May 2022 OEWS SOC vintages may not align for every code

sources.publisher: National Center for Education Statistics and Bureau of Labor Statistics
sources.join_fields: Normalized six-digit CIP and six-digit SOC
sources.transformation: Constrain exact disambiguation, safe-normalization matches, and provisional fuzzy candidates to official CIP-SOC relationships; use CIP-specific reviewed overrides where a title has different meanings across programs
sources.use: Conservative disambiguation of observed job titles
sources.limitations: The crosswalk describes occupations for which a program prepares students; it is not an observed job outcome and is never used without title evidence

sources.dataset: Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics all-area file
sources.transformation: Keep cross-industry national and state rows; parse annual percentiles; reconcile 2018-SOC consolidations to published 2022 codes and use a documented broad or minor occupation only when the detailed annual median is suppressed
sources.use: National and state occupational wage burden benchmarks
sources.limitations: Occupation-wide wages are not observed OPT salaries; parent fallbacks are less specific; one military occupation is explicitly unavailable because OEWS excludes military-specific occupations

sources.transformation: Review the 500 highest-volume unresolved clusters; validate all 198 provisional fuzzy clusters because fewer than 300 qualified; require 97% person-weighted and 95% cluster precision; demote the entire fuzzy method when either threshold fails; import a second human review of 50 high-value clusters with global scope only when all reviewed clusters for the title agree; apply a separate title-phrase plus CIP-constrained broad-family fallback using BLS OEWS major-group medians
sources.use: Audit occupation-match expansion before website use
sources.limitations: Review judgments are conservative but not ground truth; broad-family rows are not six-digit SOC outcomes; 28,960 titleless records and unresolved generic titles receive no occupation; global title decisions apply beyond the reviewed CIP rows; later jobs are never substituted

sources.transformation: Divide occupational median wage by the 2022 civilian wage share of total compensation (0.690)
sources.limitations: Civilian average benefit ratio is not occupation-, employer-, or location-specific

sources.publisher: National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics
sources.join_fields: Postdoctoral study and broad field of doctorate
sources.transformation: Use the $55,000 median basic annual salary reported for doctorate recipients with definite postdoc plans; apply the BLS ECEC wage share to estimate salary plus employer-paid benefits
sources.use: Year-matched postdoc salary and total-compensation benchmark
sources.limitations: Expected salary among new doctorate recipients with definite postdoc plans; not all established postdocs and not limited to NSF-funded positions; the benefits adjustment excludes research expenses and institutional overhead

sources.publisher: National Center for Science and Engineering Statistics
sources.dataset: Survey of Graduate Students and Postdoctorates in Science and Engineering tables 2 and 3-2
sources.transformation: Record 35,461 temporary-visa postdocs from published table 2 and read 31,643 of 62,750 postdocs with federal primary support from table 3-2
sources.use: Contextualize academic postdoc visa and primary-support populations
sources.limitations: Temporary visa is not separated into F-1, J-1, H-1B, or other classes; primary support is not average grant dollars; GSS and SEVIS universes differ

sources.local_input: Published program description in derived context table
sources.transformation: Record the official category scope without assigning a count or substitution probability
sources.use: Describe a possible J-1 research pathway
sources.limitations: Research Scholar is broader than postdoc and eligibility or sponsorship is not observed
